1. Dataset Description and Target

Summer next-day maximum temperature forecasts from Korea Meteorological Administration LDAPS across 25 Seoul weather stations (2013-2017).

Dataset-Specific Notes

  • Two trailing summary rows with missing Date/station (min/max rows in raw UCI CSV) and 27 rows with missing target 'Next_Tmax' are dropped prior to splitting.
  • 'Next_Tmin' is excluded as a co-target not available at prediction time; 'station' is excluded because station geography is captured by lat/lon/DEM/Slope.
  • Predictor missing values (~70-75 rows) are median-imputed using training-fold statistics only.
  • Chronological date-level 80/20 split ensures all stations on a given date appear together with zero same-day or future leakage.

6. Algorithm-Specific Interpretation

  • On the held-out test split (n=1538), the model achieves R²=0.6939 and RMSE=1.741 deg C (compared to Train R²=0.7838, Train RMSE=1.447 deg C).
  • Largest standardized predictor effects in absolute magnitude: LDAPS_Tmax_lapse (+1.839), Present_Tmax (+0.5107), LDAPS_RHmin (+0.4383).
  • Exact OLS identities hold to machine precision: max |X_aug^T r|=3.69e-11, |mean(y) - mean(y_hat)|=7.11e-15, and predictions match scikit-learn LinearRegression within 2.84e-14.
  • Standardizing predictors changes the augmented design matrix condition number from 9.0395e+06 (unstandardized) to 9.1055 (standardized), with rank 22 of 22.

7. Limitations and Potential Assumption Violations

  • Heteroskedasticity check rejects constant error variance (Breusch-Pagan p=1.94e-79), meaning classical homoskedastic OLS standard errors would be unreliable.
  • Training residuals deviate from Gaussian normality (Jarque-Bera p=1.93e-52, skewness=0.189, excess kurtosis=0.884).
  • 386 training observation(s) exceed the Cook's distance 4/n threshold (max Cook's D=0.01039), indicating potential sensitivity to influential points.
  • Residual autocorrelation is indicated (Durbin-Watson=0.520, lag-1 corr=0.740), violating independent-error assumptions—especially notable for ordered/time-series data.
  • Purely linear static features without explicit lag or seasonal terms may miss temporal dynamics across the chronological train-to-test shift.
  • Linear models assume additive linear relationships between standardized predictors and the conditional target mean; nonlinear interactions require basis expansion or nonlinear models.
